results.relation_rationale: Select Figure 2A's full-analysis-set adjusted OR 4.82 (95% CI 1.43–16.30), P=0.01, for the reported first hierarchical primary endpoint at 3 years: 14/82 versus 4/80. The report's prose endpoint matches the requested remission construct and time; its logistic model adjusts for baseline eGFR and proteinuria. The non-exact related classification preserves unresolved correspondence because the original protocol used proteinuria <0.2 g/day and measured clearance, later changed to g/g and CKD-EPI eGFR, while SAP section 9.2.9 prints event coding and an end-minus-baseline GFR difference inconsistent with its prose definition. Do not assume which calculation was implemented. Prefer the principal full-analysis result over the available-case sensitivity OR 5.38 (1.55–18.66), which excludes missing observations, and over the distinct second primary endpoint eGFR decrease ≥15. The latter is context, not a substitute. All inspected outcome-designation sources expressly list primary endpoints; an absence of a designated primary endpoint is not established. Current registry bytes are dated augmentation, not historical replay.

The open-label regimens were delivered by unblinded clinicians. Objective laboratory endpoints do not blind treatment delivery.

Supportive care was reported as standardized and the assigned regimens are described, but actual nonadherence, switching and reasons are not adequately reported to distinguish trial-context departures from ordinary clinical changes. The SAP disposition graphic contains planned placeholders, not performed counts. Open-label conduct or toxicity alone cannot establish context-caused deviations.

answers.justification: The selected principal result uses all 80 and 82 randomized participants in assigned groups, with missing outcome data classified as failure. unknowns: No arm-specific laboratory quality audit or remission reanalysis using clearance is supplied.

10.3 STATISTICAL METHODS
We consider the "baseline value" of GFR or proteinuria for computations of the primary and
secondary endpoints as mean value of the visit -1 week and the baseline visit. Furthermore we
will also compute the values at the end of the study period as double measurement on two
different days within one week of serum creatinine, creatinine clearance and 24h proteinuria. A
case with missing baseline GFR or baseline proteinuria will not be observed, because these
values are essential for central randomisation. Cases, where documentation does not allow
assessment of treatment success, will be defined as treatment failure with respect to the two
primary endpoints (not in full clinical remission and GFR loss of more than 15 ml/min).
Sensitivity analysis will be conducted to assess the effect of these substitution rules on the
results of the statistical evaluation.
A subsequent explorative statistical analysis will include the factor sex in the below specified
statistical models, to demonstrate possible gender specific efficacy differences.
The steering committee may suggest changes in the original statistical evaluation plan e.g.
reduction of the number of interim analyses. The study group (all physicians) will decide about
the acceptance of these changes. However, these decisions will be performed blinded to the
data.

10.3.1
PRIMARY ENDPOINTS

We will consider two primary endpoints.
